narrative:
The assessment estimated a 45% probability of bad credit, meaning roughly 45 out of 100 applicants with a similar profile would be expected to have credit problems. For this lender’s decision, that risk level was treated as too high, so the application was denied.

The most influential factor was your checking account status: it was below zero DM, and only about 12.6% of approved applicants had that status, compared with 59.2% who had no negative balance. This was the strongest driver and it pushed the assessment toward bad credit. The second most influential factor was your credit history, rated as critical or other credits; in this assessment its effect leaned toward the lower-risk side, even though it remains a concern. The third most influential factor was the requested amount of 2,121 DM, which is below the approved average of about 3,020 DM and therefore also pushed toward good credit. Even so, the negative checking account influence was strong enough that the overall decision remained denial.

To improve your chances next time, bring your checking account into positive standing and keep it there, address any critical credit-history issues, and continue keeping loan requests modest. Ask the lender what specific records or changes would strengthen a future application, and consider waiting until your account balance and credit history show a more stable pattern.
